# Prompt

> run-complexity on the pipeline

# Skill

`run-complexity` from the **ropensci-skills** plugin
(`ropensci-review-tools/ropensci-skills`, marketplace version 1.0.0, installed
2026-11-19; skill file
`~/.claude/plugins/cache/ropensci-skills/ropensci-skills/1.0.0/skills/run-complexity/SKILL.md`).
Report skeleton from the shared template
`../run-package-review/references/report-template.md` of the same plugin.

The operative instructions, verbatim:

> ## Ground rules (these make the report trustworthy)
>
> - **Measure first.** Rank functions by a real metric before reading source; the
>   eye is a poor complexity meter and misses structural duplication entirely.
> - **Read the code to interpret the numbers.** A high score can be benign
>   (a chain of `&&` guards); a low score can hide 85× duplication. The metric
>   points; you judge.
> - **Confirm behavioural claims with runtime probes.** If you say a function is
>   inert or its error path is broken, reproduce it in a scratch session and paste
>   the result.
> - **Read-only.** No refactoring the package to prove a point. Throwaway probes
>   are fine; changes to the package tree are not.
> - **Preserve the user-facing surface.** Every internal-refactor recommendation
>   must keep exported names, signatures, and return types identical. Genuine
>   API/UX changes are flagged **separately** as optional, not folded into
>   "simplification".
>
> ## Method
>
> 1. **Per-function metrics.** With `devtools::load_all()`, compute cyclomatic
>    complexity for every function in the namespace (e.g. `cyclocomp::cyclocomp()`),
>    plus lines-of-code, maximum brace-nesting depth, and `if`/`for` counts from
>    the deparsed bodies. Rank; note the distribution (most functions are usually
>    trivial — complexity concentrates in a few).
> 2. **Static call-graph.** Over `R/*.R`, use token analysis
>    (`utils::getParseData()`) to measure **duplication** (near-identical bodies)
>    and to count **call sites** of key helpers. Cyclomatic complexity is blind to
>    copy-paste across files; this is where you find it.
> 3. **Targeted source reading** of the top offenders to characterise _why_ they
>    are complex (god-function, deep nesting, repeated block) and whether it's
>    genuine or measurement artefact.
> 4. **Runtime probes** to confirm behavioural findings surfaced while measuring
>    (e.g. validation that never runs, an error path that throws the wrong error).

**Deviation from the skill, stated plainly:** `midwifery` is not an R package
(no `DESCRIPTION`, no namespace — the project is a pipeline of scripts by
design), so step 1's `devtools::load_all()` is inapplicable. Functions were
instead collected by parsing each file and evaluating only top-level
`name <- function(...)` right-hand sides in an empty environment — creating a
closure runs no body, so nothing in the pipeline executed. Step 2's
`getParseData()` token analysis was replaced by `deparse()`-based token
n-gram shingling, which gave both an identifier-level and a structure-only
(identifiers erased) similarity, so renamed copies are still detected.

# Report

## Method

Tooling: R 4.5.2 (2025-10-31), `cyclocomp` 1.1.2, `dplyr` 1.2.1, on
`refactor/ponytail-audit-cuts` @ `7cf5fad`.

**Scope — "the pipeline".** Taken as the five stages
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) labels *The pipeline*, R side only (stages 1
and 2 are Python), closed over `source()` using the repo's **own** closure
walker, `.code_closure()` in `R/lib/artifact_provenance.R:99`:

```r
source("R/lib/artifact_provenance.R")
for (s in c("match_nppes.R", "geocode_midwives.R", "check_npi_deactivation.R"))
  print(.code_closure(s))
```

| Stage | Entry | Closure |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | `match_nppes.R` | `credential_compatibility.R`, `R/lib/artifact_provenance.R`, `R/lib/provenance.R` |
| 4 | `geocode_midwives.R` | `R/lib/geocode_conflicts.R`, `R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R` |
| 5 | `check_npi_deactivation.R` | `R/join_safety.R`, `R/safe_divide.R` |

Ten files, **4,779 lines, 48 functions**.

Commands run (all read-only; scripts live in the session scratchpad, not the
repo):

```bash
# per-function metrics: cc, LOC, if/loop/apply counts, max brace depth, arity
Rscript metrics.R match_nppes.R credential_compatibility.R geocode_midwives.R \
  check_npi_deactivation.R R/lib/artifact_provenance.R R/lib/provenance.R \
  R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R R/lib/geocode_conflicts.R R/join_safety.R R/safe_divide.R

# near-duplicate bodies: 5-gram identifier Jaccard + 7-gram structure-only Jaccard
Rscript dup2.R <same file list>

# repo-wide context: every tracked .R outside tests/ and @archive/ (398 files)
Rscript metrics.R $(git ls-files '*.R' | grep -v '^tests/' | grep -v '^@archive/')

# call sites
git grep -nF 'safe_inner_join(' -- '*.R'      # etc. per helper
```

One runtime probe was run (Finding 2), in a throwaway `Rscript` session that
sourced `R/join_safety.R` and joined two three-row in-memory data frames. It
touched no pipeline input or output.

**No repository files were modified.** The only file written is this report.

## Headline

**Amber.** Per-function complexity in the pipeline is not the problem: 77% of
the repo's 956 functions score cc ≤ 5, and the pipeline's own glue
(`score_one()`, the credential gate, the geocode resolvers) is proportionate to
the decisions it makes. The problem is **mass**: `R/join_safety.R` is 1,892
lines — 40% of the pipeline's source closure — and stage 5 sources it to use
exactly **one** 69-line function from it. Three of its four `safe_*_join()`
functions (cc 55, 18, 18) have **zero production call sites**, it is a drifted
vendored fork of `~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R` (17 hunks), and it carries a
branch that can only ever `stop()` because the file it depends on was never in
this repo. Against that, the pipeline's five R stages make **8 bare `dplyr`
joins and 0 guarded ones**. Roughly **1,100 lines of the closure are
unreachable or unused**, and one of the unused four has a real defect the
duplication hid (Finding 2).

### Hotspot 1 — `R/join_safety.R` is 1,892 lines serving one 69-line call _(High.)_

Stage 5, in full (`check_npi_deactivation.R`, 65 lines), sources the module at
line 21 and uses one thing from it:

```r
source(file.path("R", "join_safety.R"))   # :21  → also pulls R/safe_divide.R (303 lines)
...
  assert_unique_keys("npi", label = "NPPES Deactivated NPI Report", dedupe = TRUE)   # :45
...
out <- midwives %>%
  left_join(select(deactivated, npi, ...), by = "npi")   # :52  — bare dplyr join
```

`assert_unique_keys()` (`R/join_safety.R:184`, cc 6, 69 LOC) calls **none** of
the module's other functions — verified by reading its body for
`safe_divide|format_by_columns|harmonize|join_coverage`: no hits. So the stage
pays **2,195 lines** of `source()` for 69, and then does its actual join
unguarded.

Call sites, production only (excluding `tests/` and the definition file):

| Function | cc | LOC | production sites | files |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `safe_left_join` | 67 | 387 | 6 | `R/01-build-county-base.R` only |
| `safe_inner_join` | 55 | 260 | **0** | tests only |
| `safe_semi_join` | 18 | 119 | **0** | tests only |
| `safe_anti_join` | 18 | 117 | **0** | tests only |

```
$ git grep -lF 'safe_inner_join(' | tr '\n' ' '
NEWS.md R/join_safety.R tests/test-join-safety-semantic-extended.R tests/test-join-safety.R tests/test_cycle9_joins.R
$ git grep -lF 'safe_semi_join(' | tr '\n' ' '
R/join_safety.R tests/test-join-safety.R tests/test_cycle9_joins.R
$ git grep -lF 'safe_anti_join(' | tr '\n' ' '
R/join_safety.R tests/test-join-safety.R tests/test_cycle9_joins.R
```

Three sub-findings compound it:

**(a) A branch that cannot succeed.** `safe_left_join(use_enhanced_metrics=)`
guards a 54-line block (`R/join_safety.R:719-772`) that calls
`safe_left_join_with_metrics()` and `log_join_integrity()`. Neither is defined
anywhere in the repo:

```
$ git grep -nE '(safe_left_join_with_metrics|log_join_integrity) *(<-|=) *function'
   (no output)
```

The file's own comment at `:628-640` says so and has already flipped the
default to `FALSE`. Every one of the **22** mentions of the parameter in the
repo passes `FALSE` explicitly — 6 in `R/01-build-county-base.R`, 16 in
`tests/test-join-safety.R`; `git grep -nE 'use_enhanced_metrics *= *TRUE'`
returns nothing. A parameter whose only reachable value is its default, gating
a block whose only reachable outcome is `stop()`.

**(b) It is a drifted fork, and the only consumer prefers the other copy.**
`R/01-build-county-base.R:82-130` defines `load_join_safety()`, which tries the
vendored copy, then `~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R`, then falls back to a
**third** implementation — a 23-line inline `safe_left_join` at `:106-128` that
keeps the same contract. Three implementations of one function in one call
path. `diff ~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R R/join_safety.R`: 17 hunks, 145
vendored-only lines, 36 upstream-only lines. (Upstream additionally defines
`.jm_ensure_metrics_loaded()` at `:600` — the machinery sub-finding (a) is dead
without.) Note also that on the vendored path the success message reads
`"Reusing safe_left_join() (vendored copy from isochrones)"`, which is not what
happened.

**(c) 17 and 16 parameters.** `safe_left_join()` takes 17 formals,
`safe_inner_join()` 16 — the arity is itself most of the cc, since each knob
brings a validation branch, an env-var fallback branch and a range-clamp
branch (`:641-705`).

**Recommended cut, user-facing surface unchanged.** Delete
`safe_inner_join()`, `safe_semi_join()` and `safe_anti_join()` and their tests;
delete the unreachable block.

> **Correction (applied 2026-11-19).** This paragraph first also recommended
> deleting the `use_enhanced_metrics` parameter and the 22 call-site arguments
> that pass `FALSE`, on the grounds that the calls "behave identically — it is
> already the default and already the only reachable value". That is true of
> the vendored copy and false of the call sites.
> `R/01-build-county-base.R:82-130` sources the vendored copy **or**
> `~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R`, and upstream (`:611-621`) defaults the same
> parameter to `TRUE` with `R/join_metrics.R` genuinely present. The six
> explicit `FALSE`s are upstream-compatibility insurance; removing them would
> silently enable the enhanced path on the upstream load, and removing the
> parameter would make every one of them an "unused argument" error. The
> parameter and its hard stop were kept; only the 54 lines of unreachable
> delegation went. Measuring one copy of a forked file and recommending for
> both is the error this correction records. That removes ~1,100
lines from the closure, retires one of the repo's five worst functions
(`safe_inner_join`, cc 55) and strips most of `safe_left_join`'s cc with it, leaving
`safe_left_join()` and `assert_unique_keys()` with identical names, signatures
(minus a parameter no caller sets to anything but its default) and return
types. Then have stage 5 source `R/join_safety.R`'s one needed function
directly, or move `assert_unique_keys()` to its own file — `assert_unique_keys`
is self-contained, so this is a file move, not a rewrite.

If any of the three unused joins is kept deliberately as a staging ground for
upstream, say so in a header comment; today nothing in the repo distinguishes
"unused on purpose" from "unused by accident".

### Hotspot 2 — `safe_anti_join()` does not harmonize key types, though its documentation says it does _(High.)_

Surfaced by the duplication scan: the semi/anti pair is 78% structurally
identical, and the diff shows exactly one guard present in one and absent in
the other.

`R/join_safety.R:1702` (the `@section Calls:` of `safe_anti_join`):

> `harmonize_join_key_types()`, `dplyr::anti_join()`, `join_coverage_report()`.

and `:1695`:

> Validates keys, harmonizes types, then calls `dplyr::anti_join(na_matches = "never")`.

The body does not:

```
$ grep -n 'harmonize_join_key_types' R/join_safety.R
88:   harmonize_join_key_types <- function(...)   # definition
711:  harmonized <- harmonize_join_key_types(...)  # safe_left_join
1197: harmonized <- harmonize_join_key_types(...)  # safe_inner_join
1523: harmonized <- harmonize_join_key_types(...)  # safe_semi_join
                                                   # safe_anti_join: absent
```

The 2026-04-05 fix (`:707-710`: "RDS/Parquet round-trips can silently change
integer→double … dplyr::left_join silently produces 0 matches") was applied to
three of the four siblings. Runtime probe — the exact shape stage 5 warns about
in its own comment at `check_npi_deactivation.R:28-30` ("NPIs are identifiers,
not numbers: read_csv infers double, the report gives character"):

```r
suppressMessages(source("R/join_safety.R"))
L <- data.frame(npi = c("1","2","3"), x = 1:3)  # character key (CSV read)
R <- data.frame(npi = 1:2)                       # integer key (parquet/RDS)
nrow(safe_semi_join(L, R, by = "npi", write_report = FALSE))
nrow(safe_anti_join(L, R, by = "npi", write_report = FALSE))
```

```
--- safe_semi_join (harmonizes) ---
[safe_join] Key type mismatch: left$npi is character, right$npi is integer — coercing both to character
📊 Semi-join: left rows=3, kept=2 (kept=66.7%)
[1] 2
--- safe_anti_join (does not) ---
[1] "ERROR: Can't join `x$npi` with `y$npi` due to incompatible types.
ℹ `x$npi` is a <character>.
ℹ `y$npi` is a <integer>."
```

It fails loudly rather than silently, which is the good failure mode — but the
documented contract is wrong, and the asymmetry is invisible to anyone reading
one function. The same gap is present upstream
(`~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R:1667-1790` has no `harmonize` call either), so
if the fix is made in the canonical copy rather than the fork, it fixes both.
This finding survives the Hotspot 1 deletion only if `safe_anti_join()` is
kept; if it goes, the fix is to the upstream copy.

### Hotspot 3 — a 98-cc CI-only static scanner sits in a library 30+ pipeline scripts source _(Medium.)_

`duckdb_scan_for_raw_connections()` (`R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R:422`, cc 98, 156
LOC, 6 nested closures, max brace depth 5) is the pipeline closure's worst
function and the repo's second worst. Reading it: it is a hand-written lint
rule — it walks each file's parse tree looking for raw `duckdb::duckdb()` /
`dbConnect()` construction, with single-assignment alias tracking, and its
boundaries are documented carefully at `:390-421`. The complexity is honest
work for what it does.

It is in the wrong file. Every caller is a gate:

```
$ git grep -n 'duckdb_scan_for_raw_connections' | grep -v '^R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R'
tests/ci_duckdb_architecture_gate.R:51
tests/ci_duckdb_exception_provenance.R:98
tests/ci_duckdb_ingestion_bootstrap.R:45
tests/ci_duckdb_mutation_tests.R:39,53,220,234,248,270
docs/TECHNICAL_APPENDIX_DUCKDB_BOOTSTRAP_ARCHITECTURE.md:125   (prose)
NEWS.md:2287                                                   (prose)
```

Zero production callers. Meanwhile `R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R` is sourced by 30+
scripts including pipeline stage 4, every one of which parses and evaluates
those 259 lines (`:356-614`, the scanner plus
`duckdb_encoding_capability()`) to get at `open_medicare_duckdb()`.

**Recommendation:** move `duckdb_scan_for_raw_connections()` (and
`DUCKDB_RAW_CONNECTION_EXCEPTIONS`) to a gate-side file the four `tests/ci_*.R`
scripts source — `tests/lib/duckdb_architecture_scan.R` or similar. Name,
signature and return value (`data.frame(file, line, tag, symbol)`) unchanged;
the four gates gain one `source()` line each and the pipeline library drops its
worst function. The mutation suite (`tests/ci_duckdb_mutation_tests.R`) already
covers the behaviour, so the move is verifiable.

### Hotspot 4 — two hand-rolled defensive AST walkers in the same closure _(Low.)_

The closure contains two independently written parse-tree walkers, both of
which exist to recurse over arbitrary R call trees without dying on R's empty
symbol:

- `walk()` inside `.code_closure()` — `R/lib/artifact_provenance.R:115-146`,
  with the comment at `:130-133`: "The gap in `x[, 1]` parses to the empty
  symbol. Binding it to a loop variable makes ANY later use of that variable
  raise 'argument is missing'…" — handled by `identical(args[i], list(quote(expr = )))`.
- `walk_calls()` inside `duckdb_scan_for_raw_connections()` —
  `R/lib/medicare_duckdb.R:458-470`, with the comment at `:446-457` making the
  same observation — handled by wrapping every recursive step in `tryCatch`.

Same problem, same closure, two solutions, two long comments explaining the
same language quirk. They are nested closures, so the cc table above attributes
their cost to their parents and the duplication scan (top-level functions only)
could not see them — a limitation of this pass worth noting.

Low priority because both work and each is read in its own context. If Hotspot
3 moves the scanner out, this resolves on its own for the pipeline; if a third
walker is ever needed, that is the signal to extract one
`walk_call_tree(node, visit)` helper into `R/lib/` and have both call it.

### Minor

- **`R/safe_divide.R`: three of six exports have no production caller.**
  `safe_divide_manu()` (0 production, 1 test), `safe_percent()` (0 production,
  **36** tests), `safe_ratio()` (0 production, 4 tests) are thin wrappers
  around `safe_divide()` that nothing in the pipeline or the repo calls;
  `safe_divide()` (11), `safe_pct_manu()` (4) and `safe_rate()` (5) are real.
  36 assertions maintaining a function with no callers is the test suite
  keeping dead flexibility alive. _(Low.)_
- **`safe_divide(na_value =)` is a second name for `default`**
  (`R/safe_divide.R:84-86`: `if (!is.null(na_value)) default <- na_value`). No
  caller in the repo passes it: `git grep -nF 'na_value =' -- '*.R'` excluding
  the definition and `tests/` returns nothing (the one hit,
  `make_migration_rate_by_method_figure.R:32`, is
  `forcats::fct_na_value_to_level`). Drop the alias; `default` stays. _(Low.)_
- **`format_by_columns()`** (`R/join_safety.R:304`, cc 25 in 48 LOC) is a
  message formatter carrying a guard per input shape (`NULL`, empty,
  `dplyr_join_by`, named character, bare character). Each guard traces to a
  numbered bug fix, so none is speculative — but if Hotspot 1 shrinks the
  module to `safe_left_join()` + `assert_unique_keys()`, the `dplyr_join_by`
  branch (`:313-329`) becomes reachable only if a caller passes `join_by()`,
  and no current caller does (all 6 pass `by = "GEOID"`). Re-check after the
  cut. _(Low.)_

### User-facing recommendations (API unchanged, but worth noting)

Kept separate from the simplifications above; all optional.

- **The guard module the pipeline does not use.** The five R pipeline stages
  make 8 bare `dplyr` joins (`match_nppes.R` 2, `geocode_midwives.R` 4,
  `check_npi_deactivation.R` 2) and 0 guarded ones, while `R/join_safety.R`
  exists to guard joins. The file's own comment at `:628-640` names the
  likeliest reason — the unusable default that made `safe_left_join()` error on
  every call — and that default is now fixed. Either adopt `safe_left_join()`
  in the stages (the row-explosion and coverage guards are exactly what a
  one-to-one NPI join wants) or state in `ARCHITECTURE.md` that the stages join
  bare on purpose. Right now the module's existence implies a convention the
  pipeline does not follow.
- **`load_join_safety()`'s success message is misleading** on the vendored
  path: `"Reusing safe_left_join() (vendored copy from isochrones)"`
  (`R/01-build-county-base.R:100`) is printed when the *local fork* loaded, not
  the isochrones copy. One-word fix, but it is the line an operator reads when
  diagnosing which of the three implementations ran.
- **Three copies invites a fourth.** Per this project's own convention that
  `~/isochrones` is canonical, the vendored fork's 145 added lines should
  either go upstream or be documented as an intentional divergence with a
  reason, so the next reader knows which copy to edit.

## Verified healthy (no action)

- **Complexity is where it should be.** The pipeline's domain glue is
  proportionate: `score_one()` (`match_nppes.R:370`, cc 27) scores one
  certificant against a surname pool, and its branches *are* the documented
  acceptance ladder — credential gate (`:378-381`), stage-1a exact match with
  the blank-name guard (`:383-393`), middle-name conflict rejection
  (`:394-398`), single-candidate-with-evidence acceptance (`:399`). That is 14
  `if`s because the contract has 14 decisions, and `ARCHITECTURE.md` points a
  newcomer at this function by name. No change.
- **`normalize_credential_class()`** (`credential_compatibility.R:35`, cc 23 in
  23 LOC) is the densest function in the closure by cc-per-line and is right:
  three matching rules (token exact, long-code substring, whole-string
  two-letter) inside one loop over credential classes, each with a comment
  saying which false match it prevents ("two-letter codes are not [matched as
  substrings], to avoid CM matching inside e.g. 'BCMA'"). The metric counts the
  loop × branch product; the code is 23 readable lines.
- **77% of the repo is trivial.** 732 of 956 functions score cc ≤ 5, median 2.
  There is no diffuse complexity problem to attack — the findings above are a
  short list on purpose.
- **The geocode layer is in proportion.** `resolve_geocode_key()` (cc 16),
  `collapse_zipless_key()` (cc 3), `summarise_geocode_resolution()` (cc 1) in
  `R/lib/geocode_conflicts.R`: one decision function, two thin helpers. This is
  what the rest of the closure should look like.
- **The closure walker exists and works.** `.code_closure()` resolved all three
  stages' `source()` graphs correctly, including the two files a manual read of
  the `source()` lines missed (`R/lib/provenance.R`, `R/safe_divide.R`). This
  pass used the repo's helper rather than writing a fourth AST walker.

## Not run (reason)

- **No pipeline stage was executed.** No `midwives.csv`, no NPI Registry calls,
  no DuckDB connection, no geocoding cache read. Functions were measured by
  parsing and closure creation only; the single runtime probe used two in-memory
  three-row data frames.
- **Python stages 1 and 2 (`scrape.py`, `fetch_npi_candidates.py`) were not
  measured.** `cyclocomp` is R-only and the skill is an R pass. Their
  complexity is unknown to this report.
- **The isochrones matching/geocoding stack was not measured.**
  `geocode_midwives.R:39-49` sources it through a runtime loop
  (`for (src in ...) source(src)`), which `.code_closure()`'s static walk cannot
  resolve, and `~/isochrones` is a separate project. `~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R`
  was read only to quantify the fork drift in Finding 1(b).
- **The other 388 tracked R files were measured but not reviewed.** They supplied
  the distribution table only. The repo's worst function overall
  (`mw_build_catalog`, cc 132, 1,344 LOC, `manuscript/R/build_stats_catalog.R:92`)
  is outside the pipeline and was not read; it would be the first stop for a
  whole-repo pass.
- **`tests/` (247 files) and `@archive/` were excluded** from all metrics. Test
  complexity was not assessed — that is `run-test-audit`'s pass.
- **Nested closures were not measured individually.** The collector takes
  top-level `name <- function(...)` only, so a nested helper's cost is
  attributed to its parent and nested bodies were excluded from the duplication
  scan. Finding 4 was found by reading, not by measuring, and there may be more
  of its kind.
- **No `getParseData()` token analysis.** Replaced by `deparse()`-based
  shingling (see Method); the two agree on what they measure, but line-accurate
  token positions were not used, so duplication findings cite function
  boundaries rather than exact repeated spans.
- **No refactor was applied and no file was changed.** Every recommendation
  above is unexecuted.

## Suggested fix priority

1. **_(High.)_ Delete the three unused `safe_*_join()` functions and the
   `use_enhanced_metrics` parameter and its unreachable block** — Hotspot 1.
   ~1,100 lines out of the pipeline closure, one of the repo's five worst
   functions gone and another cut down. Keep the `use_enhanced_metrics`
   parameter and its refusal (see the correction under Hotspot 1), so no
   production call site is affected (all are tests-only or pass
   the parameter's own default). Largest reduction, lowest risk.
2. **_(High.)_ Fix `safe_anti_join()`'s key-type contract** — Hotspot 2. Either
   add the `harmonize_join_key_types()` call its documentation promises or
   correct `R/join_safety.R:1695` and `:1702`. Fix it in `~/isochrones` (the
   canonical copy, which has the same gap) if the function survives step 1;
   otherwise fix upstream only.
3. **_(Medium.)_ Move `duckdb_scan_for_raw_connections()` to a gate-side file**
   — Hotspot 3. Removes the closure's worst function (cc 98) from a library 30+
   scripts source, with the mutation suite already in place to verify it.
4. **_(Medium.)_ Resolve the three `safe_left_join` implementations to one** —
   Hotspot 1(b). Decide whether the vendored fork or `~/isochrones` is
   authoritative, upstream the 145 divergent lines or document them, and fix the
   misleading `load_join_safety()` success message.
5. **_(Low.)_ Drop `safe_divide()`'s three uncalled wrappers and the `na_value`
   alias** — Minor. Also retires 41 test assertions that maintain code nothing
   calls.
6. **_(Low.)_ Decide the join convention and write it down** — User-facing
   recommendations. 8 bare joins against 0 guarded ones in the five stages is
   either a gap to close or a decision to record in `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
7. **_(Low.)_ One shared AST walker, if a third is ever needed** — Hotspot 4.
   Resolves itself for the pipeline if step 3 lands.

# Applied

All four were fixed on 2026-11-19, on branch `refactor/complexity-audit-fixes`,
with `tests/test_complexity_cuts_saboteurs.R` (26 assertions, four saboteurs,
each mutating what it guards and checked in both directions) and
`~/isochrones/tests/test_safe_join_key_harmonization.R`. See `NEWS.md`,
2026-11-19. Net −1,300 lines. Two things the fix pass found that this report
did not:

- **A second dead delegation, 200 lines below the first.** `safe_left_join()`
  also logged to `log_join_integrity()` behind
  `exists("log_join_integrity", mode = "function")`, inside a `tryCatch` that
  would have swallowed the error if it ever became TRUE. 17 more unreachable
  lines. This report measured one branch and read only the branch the
  measurement pointed at; the gate written for Finding 1 — which parses every
  tracked file for *calls* to functions no file defines — is what found the
  twin. A text scan would not have: the surviving `stop()` names the function
  it refuses to call.
- **The guard in Finding 4 is load-bearing against one specific idiom.** A
  walker that indexes with `[[` survives `df[, "col"]`; one that binds with
  `for (el in as.list(node)[-1L])` dies on it, which is what both originals'
  comments describe and what `C4e` now reproduces. Worth stating because a
  guard whose necessity cannot be reproduced invites its own removal.

One finding was fixed upstream rather than here: `safe_anti_join()` did not
survive Finding 1 in this repository, so the key-type fix went into
`~/isochrones/R/join_safety.R`, the canonical copy, where the function lives on
(edited locally, not committed or pushed there).
